summary: George Best Belfast City Airport (BHD) is a convenient regional airport located just 3 miles (5 km) east of Belfast city centre along the shores of Belfast Lough. Named in honour of legendary Northern Irish footballer George Best in 2006, it primarily serves domestic UK routes alongside select European destinations, offering a quicker alternative to the larger Belfast International Airport. Its compact terminal and proximity to the city make it a popular choice for business travellers and short-haul passengers.
faqs:
Q: How far is George Best Belfast City Airport from Belfast city centre?
A: The airport is approximately 3 miles (5 km) east of Belfast city centre, with a typical journey time of 10–15 minutes by car or taxi.

Q: Which airlines operate from Belfast City Airport?
A: Major carriers include Aer Lingus Regional, British Airways, easyJet, Loganair, and Ryanair, offering routes to UK cities and select European destinations.

Q: Does the airport have public transport links?
A: Yes, the Airport Express 600 bus service runs frequently between the airport, Belfast city centre, and the main transport hubs, providing a reliable and affordable connection.

Q: Are there parking facilities on-site?
A: The airport offers short-stay, long-stay, and premium parking options within walking distance of the terminal, with pre-booking available online for discounted rates.
transport_tips: The Airport Express 600 bus is the most cost-effective way to reach the city centre, running every 15–20 minutes during peak hours. Taxis are readily available outside the terminal and the short journey to central Belfast typically costs around £8–£12. If arriving by car, note that the Sydenham Bypass (A2) provides direct access to the airport from the city and motorway network.
local_tip: Time your departure to enjoy views of Belfast Lough and the Harland & Wolff cranes (home of the Titanic) during takeoff or landing — one of the most scenic approaches in UK regional aviation.
